$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}3x, & 0<x<1,\,0<y<x \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}\,{f}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}, & 0<x<1 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the continuous random variables $X$ and $Y,$ for which the joint probability density function $f(x,y)$ and the marginal density function ${f}_{X}(x)$ are shown above. Find the expression of the conditional probability density function ${f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x)$ for $0<x<1,\,0<y<x.$
q-143468.worked_solution:
Recall that the conditional probability density function of $X$ given $Y=y$ for two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by

$$
{f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)=\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{Y}(y)},
$$

where

- $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability density function for $X$ and $Y,$ and

- ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is the marginal density function for $Y.$

Now, for $0<x<1,\,0<y<x,$ we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x) & =\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{X}(x)} \\  & =\frac{3x}{3{x}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

For other values of $x$ and $y,$ the function $f(x,y)$ equals $0.$ As a result, ${f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)$ will be equal to $0$ too.

Therefore, the conditional probability density function is the following:

$$
{f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{x}, & 0<x<1,\,0<y<x \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
{f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x)=\{\begin{aligned}3{e}^{-3y}, & 0\le x\le 1,\,y\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}\,{f}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}2x, & 0\le x\le 1 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the continuous random variables $X$ and $Y,$ for which the conditional probability density function ${f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x)$ and the marginal density function ${f}_{X}(x)$ are shown above. Find the expression of the joint probability density function $f(x,y)$ for $0\le x\le 1,\,y\ge 0.$
q-143613.worked_solution:
Recall that the conditional probability density function of $Y$ given $X=x$ for two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by

$$
{f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x)=\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{X}(x)},
$$

where

- $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability density function for $X$ and $Y,$ and

- ${f}_{X}(x)$ is the marginal density function for $X.$

From the equation above, it follows that

$$
f(x,y)={f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x)\cdot {f}_{X}(x).
$$

Now, for $0\le x\le 1,\,y\ge 0,$ we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y) & ={f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x)\cdot {f}_{X}(x) \\  & =3{e}^{-3y}\cdot 2x \\  & =6x{e}^{-3y}.\end{aligned}
$$

For other values of $x$ and $y,$ the function ${f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x)$ equals $0.$ As a result, the product will be equal to $0$ too.

Therefore, the joint probability density function is the following:

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}6x{e}^{-3y}, & 0\le x\le 1,\,y\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the continuous random variables $X$ and $Y,$ for which the joint probability density function $f(x,y)$ and the marginal density function ${f}_{X}(x)$ are shown above. Find the expression of the conditional probability density function ${f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x)$ for $0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 3.$
q-144941.worked_solution:
Recall that the conditional probability density function of $Y$ given $X=x$ for two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by

$$
{f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x)=\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{X}(x)},
$$

where

- $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability density function for $X$ and $Y,$ and

- ${f}_{X}(x)$ is the marginal density function for $X.$

Now, for $0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 3,$ we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x) & =\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{X}(x)} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}{10})}{(\frac{3{x}^{2}+9}{10})} \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}{3{x}^{2}+9}.\end{aligned}
$$

For other values of $x$ and $y,$ the function $f(x,y)$ equals $0.$ As a result, ${f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x)$ will be equal to $0$ too.

Therefore, the conditional probability density function is the following:

$$
{f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}{3{x}^{2}+9}, & 0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 3 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

$$

where

$$

q-145095.name: Question 6
q-145095.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the following joint probability density function:

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{xy+1}{3}, & \,0\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le 1 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Find the expression of the conditional probability density function ${f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)$ for $0\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le 1.$
q-145095.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the marginal density function for $Y,$ we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(y) & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{xy+1}{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{\int }_{0}^{2}(xy+1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{[\frac{{x}^{2}y}{2}+x]}_{x=0}^{x=2} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot [2y+2-0] \\  & =\frac{2(y+1)}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the full expression for ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is the following:

$$
{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2(y+1)}{3}, & \,0\le x\le 2 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Now recall that the conditional probability density function of $X$ given $Y=y$ for two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by

$$
{f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)=\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{Y}(y)},
$$

where

- $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability density function for $X$ and $Y,$ and

- ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is the marginal density function for $Y.$

Now, for $0\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le 1,$ we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y) & =\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{Y}(y)} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{xy+1}{3})}{(\frac{2(y+1)}{3})} \\  & =\frac{xy+1}{2(y+1)}.\end{aligned}
$$

For other values of $x$ and $y,$ the function $f(x,y)$ equals $0.$ As a result, ${f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)$ will be equal to $0$ too.

Therefore, the conditional probability density function is the following:

$$
{f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{xy+1}{2(y+1)}, & \,0\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le 1 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

q-143640.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the following joint probability density function:

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{3x}{8}, & \,0\le x<2,\,{x}^{2}\le y\le x+2 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Find the expression of the conditional probability density function ${f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x)$ for $0\le x<2,\,{x}^{2}\le y\le x+2.$
q-143640.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the marginal density function for $X,$ we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x) & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{x+2}\frac{3x}{8}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{3x}{8}\cdot y\,{|}_{{x}^{2}}^{x+2} \\  & =\frac{3x}{8}\cdot (x+2-{x}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{3x(-{x}^{2}+x+2)}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the full expression for ${f}_{X}(x)$ is the following:

$$
{f}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{3x(-{x}^{2}+x+2)}{8}, & \,0\le x<2 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Now recall that the conditional probability density function of $Y$ given $X=x$ for two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by

$$
{f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x)=\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{X}(x)},
$$

where

- $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability density function for $X$ and $Y,$ and

- ${f}_{X}(x)$ is the marginal density function for $X.$

Now, for $0\le x<2,\,{x}^{2}\le y\le x+2,$ we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x) & =\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{X}(x)} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{3x}{8})}{(\frac{3x(-{x}^{2}+x+2)}{8})} \\  & =\frac{1}{-{x}^{2}+x+2}.\end{aligned}
$$

For other values of $x$ and $y,$ the function $f(x,y)$ equals $0.$ As a result, ${f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x)$ will be equal to $0$ too.

Therefore, the conditional probability density function is the following:

$$
{f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{-{x}^{2}+x+2}, & \,0\le x<2,\,{x}^{2}\le y\le x+2 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the following joint probability density function:

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{{e}^{x+y}}{2}, & \,0\le x\le \operatorname{ln}⁡3,\,0\le y\le \operatorname{ln}⁡2 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}

Using the formula for the marginal density function for $X,$ we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x) & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\frac{{e}^{x+y}}{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{{e}^{x}}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{e}^{y}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{{e}^{x}}{2}\cdot {e}^{y}\,{|}_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{x}}{2}\cdot (2-1) \\  & =\frac{{e}^{x}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the full expression for ${f}_{X}(x)$ is the following:

$$
{f}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{{e}^{x}}{2}, & \,0\le x\le \operatorname{ln}⁡3 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Now recall that the conditional probability density function of $Y$ given $X=x$ for two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by

$$
{f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x)=\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{X}(x)},
$$

where

- $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability density function for $X$ and $Y,$ and

- ${f}_{X}(x)$ is the marginal density function for $X.$

Now, for $0\le x\le \operatorname{ln}⁡3,\,0\le y\le \operatorname{ln}⁡2,$ we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x) & =\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{X}(x)} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{{e}^{x+y}}{2})}{(\frac{{e}^{x}}{2})} \\  & ={e}^{y}.\end{aligned}

$$

q-145127.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the following joint probability density function:

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{3(x+2y)}{2}, & \,0\le y\le x\le 1 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Find $P(X<\frac{2}{5}\,|\,Y=\frac{1}{5}).$
q-145127.worked_solution:
Recall that 

$$
P(Y\in A\,|\,X=x)={\int }_{A}{f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)\,\text{d}y,
$$

where ${f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)$ is the conditional probability density function of $X$ given $Y=y.$ 

Using the formula for the marginal density function for $Y,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(y) & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{y}^{1}\frac{3(x+2y)}{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{2}{\int }_{y}^{1}(x+2y)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{2}{[\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}+2xy]}_{x=y}^{x=1} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}(\frac{1}{2}+2y-\frac{1}{2}{y}^{2}-2{y}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{3}{2}[\frac{1+4y-5{y}^{2}}{2}] \\  & =\frac{3(1+4y-5{y}^{2})}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the full expression for ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is the following:

$$
{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{3(1+4y-5{y}^{2})}{4}, & \,0\le y\le 1 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Now recall that the conditional probability density function of $X$ given $Y=y$ for two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by

$$
{f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)=\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{Y}(y)}.
$$

where

- $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability density function for $X$ and $Y,$ and

- ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is the marginal density function for $Y.$

Now, for $0\le y\le x\le 1,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y) & =\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{Y}(y)} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{3(x+2y)}{2})}{(\frac{3(1+4y-5{y}^{2})}{4})} \\  & =\frac{2(x+2y)}{1+4y-5{y}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

For other values of $x$ and $y,$ the function $f(x,y)$ equals $0.$ As a result, ${f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)$ will be equal to $0$ too.

Therefore, the conditional probability density function is the following:

$$
{f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2(x+2y)}{1+4y-5{y}^{2}}, & \,0\le y\le x\le 1 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

q-143624.name: Question 14
q-143624.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the following joint probability density function:

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}2x{e}^{y}, & \,0\le x\le 1,0\le y\le \operatorname{ln}⁡2 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Find $P(X<Y\,|\,X=\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{3}{2})).$
q-143624.worked_solution:
Recall that 

$$
P(Y\in A\,|\,X=x)={\int }_{A}{f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x)\,\text{d}y,
$$

where ${f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x)$ is the conditional probability density function of $Y$ given $X=x.$ 

Using the formula for the marginal density function for $X,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x) & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}2x{e}^{y}\,\text{d}y \\  & =2x{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{e}^{y}\,\text{d}y \\  & =2x{[{e}^{y}]}_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2} \\  & =2x(2-1) \\  & =2x.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the full expression for ${f}_{X}(x)$ is the following:

$$
{f}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}2x, & \,0\le x\le 1 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Now recall that the conditional probability density function of $Y$ given $X=x$ for two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by

$$
{f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x)=\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{X}(x)}.
$$

where

- $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability density function for $X$ and $Y,$ and

- ${f}_{X}(x)$ is the marginal density function for $X.$

Now, for $0<x<1,0<y<\operatorname{ln}⁡2,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x) & =\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{X}(x)} \\  & =\frac{2x{e}^{y}}{2x} \\  & ={e}^{y}.\end{aligned}
$$

For other values of $x$ and $y,$ the function $f(x,y)$ equals $0.$ As a result, ${f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x)$ will be equal to $0$ too.

Therefore, the conditional probability density function is the following:

$$
{f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x)=\{\begin{aligned}{e}^{y}, & \,0\le y\le \operatorname{ln}⁡2 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we compute our probability:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<Y\,|\,X=\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{3}{2})) & =P(\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{3}{2})<Y\,|\,X=\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{3}{2})) \\  & ={\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡(3/2)}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x=\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{3}{2}))\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡(3/2)}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{e}^{y}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[{e}^{y}]}_{\operatorname{ln}⁡(3/2)}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2} \\  & =2-\frac{3}{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-145119.name: Question 15
q-145119.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the following joint probability density function:

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{x+y}{3}, & \,0\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le 1 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Find $P(X<\frac{2}{3}\,|\,Y=\frac{1}{2}).$
q-145119.worked_solution:
Recall that 

$$
P(Y\in A\,|\,X=x)={\int }_{A}{f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)\,\text{d}y,
$$

where ${f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)$ is the conditional probability density function of $X$ given $Y=y.$ 

Using the formula for the marginal density function for $Y,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(y) & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{x+y}{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{\int }_{0}^{2}(x+y)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{[\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+xy]}_{x=0}^{x=2} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(2+2y-0) \\  & =\frac{2(y+1)}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the full expression for ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is the following:

$$
{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2(y+1)}{3}, & \,0\le y\le 1 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Now recall that the conditional probability density function of $X$ given $Y=y$ for two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by

$$
{f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)=\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{Y}(y)}.
$$

where

- $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability density function for $X$ and $Y,$ and

- ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is the marginal density function for $Y.$

Now, for $0\le x\le 2,0\le y\le 1,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y) & =\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{Y}(y)} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{x+y}{3})}{(\frac{2(y+1)}{3})} \\  & =\frac{x+y}{2(y+1)}.\end{aligned}
$$

For other values of $x$ and $y,$ the function $f(x,y)$ equals $0.$ As a result, ${f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)$ will be equal to $0$ too.

Therefore, the conditional probability density function is the following:

$$
{f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{x+y}{2(y+1)}, & \,0\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le 1 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we compute our probability:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<\frac{2}{3}\,|\,Y=\frac{1}{2}) & ={\int }_{0}^{2/3}{f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y=\frac{1}{2})\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2/3}\frac{(x+\frac{1}{2})}{2(\frac{1}{2}+1)}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{6}{\int }_{0}^{2/3}(2x+1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{6}{[{x}^{2}+x]}_{0}^{2/3} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}(\frac{4}{9}+\frac{2}{3}-0) \\  & =\frac{1}{6}(\frac{10}{9}) \\  & =\frac{5}{27}.\end{aligned}
$$
